advice.good: Air quality is satisfactory. Enjoy outdoor activities normally!
advice.moderate: Air quality is acceptable. Very sensitive individuals should observe for irritation.
advice.unhealthy: Reduce outdoor activities. Sensitive groups should wear an N95 mask outdoors.
advice.veryUnhealthy: Avoid outdoor activities! Wear N95 masks, close windows, and run air purifiers.
advice.hazardous: DANGER: Stay indoors strictly! Seal doors and windows. Follow official emergency guidance.

danger.title: High respiratory sensitivity
danger.text: Keep reliever inhaler accessible and remain indoors. Keep windows closed and run an air purifier if available.

warning.title: Fine particles irritating airways
warning.text: Limit prolonged outdoor exertion. Have prescribed preventers or inhalers nearby if chest tightness develops.

good.title: Airway conditions favorable
good.text: Particulate levels are within normal limits. Maintain regular daily routines.

danger.title: Official MOE closure threshold reached
danger.text: Children should stay indoors. Keep classroom windows closed and avoid outdoor transit.

warning.title: Outdoor activities restricted
warning.text: Schools and preschools should move physical activities, field trips, and playground sessions indoors.

good.title: Normal playground activities safe
good.text: Children can play outside freely in physical education and playground sessions.

warning.title: Cardiovascular caution window
warning.text: Limit early morning and late evening strolls when haze settles near ground level. Stay well-hydrated indoors.

good.title: Ideal for morning walks and garden time
good.text: Air quality is good. Great conditions for senior strolls and fresh outdoor leisure.

danger.title: Postpone strenuous outdoor exercise
danger.text: Vigorous breathing draws smoke particles deep into your lungs. Move running, cycling, or football sessions indoors.

warning.title: Reduce intense outdoor workouts
warning.text: Shorten runs to under 30 minutes at an easy pace, or shift intense training indoors.

good.title: Prime air quality for outdoor training
good.text: No respiratory restrictions. Ideal conditions for long runs, cycling, and outdoor recreation.

hotspots.subtitle: Satellite fire count & transboundary haze watch
hotspots.trendWarning: Haze trajectory deteriorating over past 3 hours
hotspots.trendImproving: Haze trajectory improving over past 3 hours
hotspots.practicalTipElevated: 💨 Southwest wind is pushing Sumatra peat smoke across the Straits. Dry laundry indoors & keep N95 masks ready.
hotspots.practicalTipModerate: ⚠️ Moderate fire activity detected in the region. Monitor wind shifts if you have respiratory sensitivity.
hotspots.practicalTipLow: ✅ Low regional fire activity and favorable air dispersion. Safe for regular outdoor routines.
hotspots.guideSubtitle: How satellite fire detections forecast upcoming haze for Malaysia
hotspots.whatIsAsmcDesc: The ASEAN Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC) uses NOAA and NASA weather satellites with thermal infrared cameras to detect active forest and peatland fires ('hotspots') across Southeast Asia.
hotspots.scaleHigh: 500+: Severe regional crisis (Dense smoke & widespread school alerts)
hotspots.whyWindMattersDesc: Fires alone do not cause haze unless the wind pushes the smoke towards us. During the Southwest Monsoon (June–October), prevailing winds act like an atmospheric conveyor belt, blowing thick peat smoke from Sumatra directly into the Klang Valley, Penang, and the West Coast.
hotspots.decisionsTitle: What This Means For Your Day
hotspots.decisionLaundryDesc: Dry clothes indoors when Sumatra fires are high and winds blow Southwest; otherwise clothes absorb strong smoky odors.
hotspots.decisionSportsDesc: A rising trajectory + Southwest wind means outdoor cardio will stress lungs. Move runs and football games indoors.
hotspots.decisionMasksDesc: Gives you a 24-hour head start to purchase N95/KF94 masks and replace air purifier filters before pharmacy shelves empty.
hotspots.decisionSchoolsDesc: Helps parents anticipate whether schools will cancel outdoor recess or if the MOE API > 200 closure rule might trigger soon.
